identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is an inspection log for a Toyota propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse, recording daily pre-shift safety checks for September 2026 against OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). The log tracks twelve checklist items per shift and identifies defects that would make the truck unsafe to operate. As a record, its value depends on completeness and timeliness of entries and whether defects are resolved before reuse.
scan.freshness_note: This log covers September 2026 and the last entry is 2026-09-18 (9 days old as of 2026-09-27). Ask whether inspections have continued through today and whether the September 3–6 gap and the unresolved horn defect from September 9 have been addressed.

gaps.title: Missing inspections Sep 3–6
gaps.description: The log shows entries for Sep 1–2, then jumps to Sep 7. The hour meter proves the truck ran during this gap (4,819 hours on Sep 2 to 4,834 on Sep 7 = 15 hours of operation). OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) requires examination before each shift. No inspections are recorded for Sep 3, 4, 5, or 6.
gaps.fix: Locate and attach any inspection records for Sep 3–6. If none exist, document the dates the truck was used on those days, explain why inspections were not recorded, and confirm with supervisors and operators that inspections occurred but were not logged. Going forward, ensure an entry appears for every day the truck operates.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'Before being put into use and at least daily, powered industrial trucks shall be examined by the person designated to operate the truck to ensure that the truck is in safe operating condition.'
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Horn defect not resolved before reuse
gaps.description: On Sep 9, operator M.C. marked the horn with an X (defect) and noted 'Horn not working.' The same truck (FL-2) was inspected and passed on Sep 10 with all items marked OK, including the horn. There is no record that the horn was repaired between Sep 9 and Sep 10. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) states: 'do not use if a defect affects safety.' The horn is a safety-critical item for warning pedestrians. Use of the truck on Sep 10 and thereafter without evidence of repair violates this rule.
gaps.fix: Obtain maintenance records showing the horn was repaired and tested as safe between the Sep 9 defect entry and the Sep 10 clearance. If no repair occurred, the Sep 10–18 entries are invalid. Document the repair date and who performed it, and update the log to show 'X' with a note 'repaired [date]' on Sep 9, or show the truck taken out of service until repair was confirmed.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'do not use if a defect affects safety'
gaps.quote: Sep 9: Horn marked X with note 'Horn not working'; Sep 10: Horn marked OK with no note of repair

gaps.title: Supervisor review signature missing
gaps.description: The log includes a line for 'Supervisor review:' with space for a signature and date (page 2). Both fields are blank. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) does not explicitly require a supervisor signature on daily inspection logs; however, OSHA guidance expects inspection records to be reviewed for compliance. Oregon administrative rules OAR 437-004-0750 (Powered Industrial Truck Operation and Maintenance) may impose additional state-level requirements. Company safety procedures may also mandate this. Without a signed supervisor review, there is no evidence that anyone with authority has verified the accuracy of the log or taken action on the defects noted.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor review the entire log for September 2026, sign and date the review line, and document any actions taken on the horn defect or missing Sep 3–6 entries. Verify whether Oregon OAR or company policy requires this; if so, make it a standing procedure for monthly logs going forward.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (does not explicitly require signature, but review is expected); Oregon OAR 437-004-0750 (verify applicability)
